description: One of Lebanon's largest listed commercial banks (est. 1950), full-service retail, corporate, private and correspondent banking with a regional branch network (Cyprus, Iraq, Armenia, Belgium, UK, Nigeria/rep offices, Syria) and its own investment-bank subsidiary (Byblos Invest Bank). Listed on the CMA Lebanon approved-institutions register for securities/investment activities. Chairman & General Manager: Semaan François Bassil (since 2015). Continues visible digital investment (launched 'BO2' digital bank platform, Feb 2025).

fit.reasoning: Fit: priority segment private/investment bank (20) + priority market Lebanon (15) + multi-asset via investment-bank subsidiary and correspondent/treasury activity (10) + manages third-party deposits and private-banking assets (10) + regulated by BDL and CMA Lebanon (5) = 60/60. Timing: Lebanon-wide regulatory trigger is real (secrecy lift Apr-2025, Law 23/2025 bank-resolution framework forcing every bank to re-prove books to a regulator with new oversight powers) = 10/25 for 'regulatory change creating reporting pressure' - NOT scored as a positive buying trigger because Byblos's individual survivor-vs-resolution status under Law 23/2025 is not publicly confirmed as of this research (2026-09-22); a bank on the liquidation track buys nothing, so this is a gating question, not a tailwind, until resolved. Continued digital investment (BO2 launch, Feb 2025) is a mild going-concern signal but not proof of survivor-track status. Access: named Chairman/GM identified (Semaan Bassil) but no direct contact route or LinkedIn profile found for him, and no other named operations/compliance contact = 3/15 (generic route only). Total 73 by table mechanics, deliberately held down to 52 (worth a look, not strong) pending the viability-track question -- Andre must confirm which track Byblos is on before any outreach effort.
